title: 41/128 route_v1 eval utterances are verbatim generation-prompt examples
detail: G1 injects each skill's catalog `examples` (skills/catalog.json:13-102) and G2/G3 inject the SPEC/CATEGORIES examples (prompts.py:64-84, G3 :40) into teacher prompts. 27 eval items equal catalog examples and 14 more equal SPEC/prompt examples, so 41/128 (32%) of evals/route_v1.jsonl are seeded into training generation; teachers echo them back. route_v1 accuracy will measure memorization of the eval set, and some echoes carry conflicting labels, so reported route numbers are contaminated either way.
evidence: Normalized exact match of evals/route_v1.jsonl@746450c vs catalog examples: lines 9,16,18,19,24,29,36,38,40,43,47,50,56,60,61,65,66,68,69,72,73,74,76,77,78,79,82 (27/69 catalog examples). vs SPEC/prompts quoted examples: lines 8 'a bit more',81 'undo that',88,89,99 'cut this',100 'set a timer',101 'text him',102,103,108,110,111,114,116. Generated sample training/artifacts/gen_sample2_picked.jsonl (1,080 rows) already has 15 exact eval hits, e.g. eval:50 'take a screenshot' (take_screenshot) generated as premiere_command; eval:80 'play it' (premiere_command) generated as ASK; eval:68 'play' generated as media_control AND premiere_command.

Either author a fresh held-out route_v2 (none of its texts in catalog.json examples, SPEC.md, prompts.py) and demote route_v1 to a dev set, or replace the 41 prompt examples with new ones. Add a postprocess assertion: normalized(utterance) not in {normalized eval utterances} else hard fail.

title: Spec 8-gram eval filter cannot match short items; no dedup/split code
detail: Word 8-gram Jaccard is undefined/zero for texts under 8 words: 100/128 route_v1 items and 542/1,080 sampled generated items are <8 words, so the specified filter removes nothing where leakage actually is (training-1). The branch has no exact-dedupe, MinHash, eval/HobbyLM-frozen filter or grouped 97/3 split code yet (git grep -nE 'minhash|dedup|97|val' training/src -> no hits; postprocess.py only writes route/args/rejects). Split grouping as specified (near-dup only) would also put the two contexts of one G3 text (postprocess.py:184-187 adds both) and future noise/follow-up variants of the same source on both sides of train/val.
evidence: Running the spec filter (word 8-gram Jaccard>=0.6) of gen_sample2_picked.jsonl vs evals/route_v1.jsonl: 0 removals; normalized exact match on the same data: 15 hits (see training-1).
fix: Eval filter = exact normalized match OR n-gram Jaccard with n=min(8,len(tokens)) (or char 5-gram Jaccard>=0.6) against evals/*.jsonl, HobbyLM data/frozen and DeskMind Bench texts. Split group key = (src call id, normalized text) so G3 pairs, noise and follow-up variants share a split. Add a test asserting zero normalized-text overlap train/val and train/eval.

title: G3 context pairs mostly mislabeled: 21/37 sampled items wrong
detail: G3 forces 'two contexts that lead to two different handlings' for every text, so gpt-5.4-nano invents a second label even when context changes nothing; postprocess.py:181 only rejects identical labels. G3 also emits arg-requiring skills with no args in the text (should be ASK). At full scale G3 is 3,000 examples (~6.5% of route data) with 0.6 weight on the intended (wrong) label, and several directly contradict G1 and the eval. Same sample also has ASK 9/30 fully specified (generated before the lead's ASK near-miss text change; re-check) and REFUSE 3/30 benign.
evidence: gen_sample2_picked.jsonl G3 rows (37): wrong = 'turn it up'->set_volume (no level), 'switch dark mode'->set_brightness, 'darker'->set_brightness, 'what's my battery?'@Calendar->todays_agenda, 'open downloads'@Safari->open_url, 'open this file'@Mail->open_url, 'open url https://example.com'@Finder->web_search, 'type hello'@Safari->web_search, 'search the web for cats'@Finder->find_file, 'make a new folder'->new_folder, 'trash this'@TextEdit->type_text, 'start a timer'->start_timer (eval:100 'set a timer'=ASK), 'add an event'->create_event and ->compose_email, 'set a reminder'->create_reminder, 'send a message to Alex'->send_message and ->compose_email, 'compose email to Jamie'->send_message and ->compose_email (no body), 'new note'->type_text, 'take a screenshot'@Premiere->premiere_command (eval:50 = take_screenshot). ASK wrong: 'Please switch to dark mode if possible.', 'Please open the Downloads folder for me.', 'Please turn Wi-Fi off for a minute.', 'What's my battery percentage right now?', 'Can you tell me my battery status, please?', 'Please center the front window.', 'Can you read my agenda for today, please?', 'Would you resize it to the right half, please?', 'Please take a screenshot and save it somewhere on the Desktop.'
fix: Let G3 return pairs only when handling truly differs (allow 'b': null, drop singletons); run A1 adjudication on 100% of G3 items (~3k Sonnet calls) and on ASK; postprocess: label an arg skill only if every required arg is present else ASK; reject ASK when nearest_skill has zero required args. title: Runtime special-option descriptions differ from training: 0/50 token parity
detail: Runtime hardcodes short descriptions for MULTI_STEP/ASK/REFUSE/ANSWER, while training (catalog.py:36-37@746450c) uses skills/catalog.json special_options (lines 5-8). title: Teacher defaults to 397B on full set with no cost guard
detail: TEACHER defaults to Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, --limit defaults to None (whole route.jsonl), concurrency 64, and nothing estimates or caps cost before asyncio.gather; the SPEC 1.4 '$15 extrapolation -> 35B' rule lives only in prose. Each item is an independent sample_decision call; whether the 20% cached-prefill discount is applied is unverified. Route datums are ~803-817 tokens (artifact), not the ~520 SPEC 1.6 assumes, so training is also ~47% dearer than budgeted.
evidence: 45K route x 800 tok = 36.0M; 397B uncached 36.0M x $1.65/M = $59.4 (alone ~= Phase-1 cap); cached prefix (770 static tok @20%) = 45K x (770x0.33+30x1.65)/1e6 = $13.7. 35B: $16.2 uncached / $3.7 cached. Training/epoch: 36.0M + 25K args x 150 = 39.8M x $0.737 = $29.3 (SPEC: 27.1M, $20). Pilots 2 LRs x 4,000 items mixed ~2.2M tok = $3.2; val evals (1,350 x 800 tok prefill $0.33) x 11/epoch = $3.9. Phase 1 total: 397B uncached ~$96 (> $60), 397B cached ~$50, 35B ~$41-53.
fix: teacher.py: require --limit or --max-usd; before sampling compute est = sum(len(render_route(...).tokens)) x price (cached/uncached) and abort if est > remaining Phase-1 budget; default TEACHER to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B unless the 500-item pilot's billed cost (tinker billing) extrapolates <= $15. Update SPEC 1.6 sizing to ~800 tok/route datum.

title: Contexts sampled independently of label contradict context-dependent supervision
detail: Every G1 item gets a uniformly random app/selection (as SPEC 1.3 says), so context-dependent skills are trained in contexts where they are wrong, while G3 trains the opposite rule. The router learns to ignore app/selection, which G3 and the demo (Premiere vs Music 'play', 'copy this' with no selection) depend on. Separately, every sampled open_url request contains a literal URL, unlike speech.
evidence: gen_sample2_picked.jsonl: premiere_command G1 26/27 with app != Premiere Pro ('hit play'@Safari, 'could you undo the last thing I did'@TextEdit, 'add a marker'@Notes) vs G3 'play'@Music -> media_control; copy_selection 23/29 with selection=no ('copy this'); open_url 27/27 contain 'http' (eval:36 'open youtube').
fix: Needs a lead SPEC decision: per-skill context priors in contexts.py (premiere_command -> app=Premiere Pro >=90%; copy_selection/deictic 'this/that' -> selection=yes; type_text -> focused text field), or drop G1 items whose context contradicts the label. G1 open_url: spoken site names, no URLs.

title: ARGS targets fabricate unspoken values, incl. destructive move_to_trash paths
detail: G1 asks for args alongside heavy phrasing variation (indirect needs), and postprocess accepts whatever the teacher writes. ARGS targets contain values the user never said, so the ARGS model learns to invent file paths for a delete skill and message bodies the user did not dictate, and relative requests become absolute.
evidence: gen_sample2_picked.jsonl: move_to_trash 28/29 path args start with '~/' not spoken (e.g. 'the old draft, the one in Pages' -> path '~/Documents/old...'); compose_email 13/27 bodies with >50% words absent from the utterance ('Aunt Rose wanted to know if we're coming for the holidays.' -> body 'Yes, we're coming for the ho...'); 'Make it 10 percent quieter' -> set_volume level=90 (should be change_volume delta=-10).
fix: postprocess: reject/route-to-ASK items where any free-text arg (path, body, title, query) is not mostly (>=80% tokens) contained in the utterance; keep enum/number/datetime normalization; indirect compose_email without dictated content -> ASK (or drop); add a rule check that 'percent quieter/louder' maps to change_volume.

title: Adjudication verdicts never applied; 15% per-label STOP not computed
detail: collect() only attaches r['adjudication'] and writes *_adj.jsonl; nothing relabels/drops adjudicated items or recomputes target, and teacher.py:53 already blended 0.6*onehot(intended) for flagged items, so a 'teacher was right' verdict changes nothing in training data. SPEC 1.3 ASR noise (30%, code) and 5% follow-up variants also have no code yet (only a style string at prompts.py:56).
evidence: adjudicate.py:59-73 sets r['adjudication'] and writes rows unchanged otherwise; git grep -nE 'adjudication\]|15|rate' training/src -> no consumer; git grep -nE 'noise|homophone|follow' training/src -> prompts.py:56 only.

title: ARGS datums bypass dedup/eval filter/split, leaking route labels
detail: dedup.py only processes route rows (keys on r['label']; args.jsonl rows carry 'skill', so --in args.jsonl raises KeyError) and writes only route_train/val. args.jsonl (1,353 rows vs 1,658 route in the 2% sample, i.e. most skill items have an ARGS twin) keeps every utterance, including those dropped for eval overlap and those assigned to route val. The ARGS user message starts with `Skill: {name}(...)` (route_render.py:39-41), so training on ARGS datums teaches utterance -> skill name for val and eval utterances: val route accuracy (used for LR pick and checkpoint selection) and any residual eval overlap are inflated, and ARGS exact match has no held-out set.
evidence: dedup.py:66 `k = (norm(r['utterance']), r['label'], ...)`; :125-127 writes route_{train,val}.jsonl only; postprocess.py args rows = {'skill','utterance','context','target','src'}; route_render.py:39 `ARGS_USER = """Skill: {name}({signature})`.
fix: Run args rows through the same pipeline keyed by (src, normalized utterance): drop args rows whose utterance was dropped from route (eval overlap/dup), and assign each args row the split of its route twin (same src+utterance); write args_train/args_val and report ARGS exact match on args_val. Add a test: no normalized utterance appears in both {route,args}_train and {route,args}_val.

title: Eval filter silently runs without HobbyLM tests and on stale route_v1
detail: HOBBY=/data/evals/hobbylm/data/frozen: if the clone is missing, glob() yields nothing and the run reports success with no HobbyLM filtering; nothing records how many eval texts were loaded. eval_texts() reads REPO/evals of the checkout it runs in, and cloud/data-pipeline still has the pre-ea64ce3 route_v1, so new route_v1 items are never filtered. DeskMind Bench/macOSWorld/MacAgentBench task texts (AGENTS.md) are not included.

title: New ctx contract makes Finder selection=yes unreachable; training uses it
detail: Contract now defines selection = focused element has non-empty AXSelectedText. Selected files in Finder are not AXSelectedText, so at runtime Finder selection is always 'no', while training labels Finder deictic requests by selection=yes (G3 'trash this'->move_to_trash, 'open this file'/'open the first result'->open_file). Normalize app names to the training set in the app (map bundle id -> 'Premiere Pro') and add a route_v1 case with Finder selection=yes.

title: topk teacher gives every out-of-top-20 option the k-th logprob
detail: --method topk assigns each of the 36 choice ids missing from the top-20 vocabulary tokens the 20th logprob (an upper bound), so uncertain items spread spurious mass across ~16-30 absent options; e.g. 30 absent ids at floor -6 add 30*e^-6 ~= 0.074 probability that never existed, and after blending 0.4*teacher it flattens targets and inflates teacher entropy/ECE. Default is chunked (exact), so this only bites if topk is used to save cost.
evidence: teacher.py@4cbb74a topk_decision: `floor = min(got.values())`; `lp = torch.tensor([got.get(rendering.label_tokens[x], floor) ...])`.
fix: Renormalize over present ids only and give absent ids 0 (or floor - log(n_absent)); or keep chunked as the only method for soft labels.

title: ask_rule relabels unclear-referent ASK ('send it to him') as concrete
detail: verdict() returns 'ask' only when the ARGS labeler outputs missing=. ARGS_SYSTEM (route_render.py:37) only says 'If a required argument is missing, reply missing=', so a pronoun or deictic phrase is copied as a value and the item becomes 'concrete'. datums.route_items then relabels it to nearest_skill with one-hot targets. Half of the new terse-ASK generator asks for exactly these items (IT2_ASK_STYLE, gen.py:153: 'point at something unclear like it, him, the one from earlier'), and the ASK definition says 'referent is unclear' (prompts.py:71). The router learns that 'send it to him' means send_message to="him" and 'play the one from earlier' means play_music. This undoes H2 for unclear-referent ASK and teaches the router to act on unresolved references. The rule (ASK when a required arg is missing) is the lead's; this concerns how the rule treats copied pronouns.
evidence: Repro at 70b7d1b: verdict(['to','body'], 'to="him" body="it"', []) == 'concrete'; verdict(['query'], 'query="the one from earlier"', []) == 'concrete'. Nothing in ask_rule or the ARGS prompt maps pronouns to missing. Skills with no required args take the `if not req: return 'concrete'` path, so the deictic 'do that one again' with nearest_skill=screenshot becomes screenshot. Not checked against real labeler output; ask_rule.json 'concrete' examples would show it.
fix: In verdict(), treat a value as missing if norm(value) is in {it, him, her, them, that, this, there, the one, the one from earlier, ...} or matches ^(it|that|this|those|these|him|her|them)\b; keep the it2 pointer-ASK requests (id g2-ASK-it2-*) out of the concrete relabel; and read ask_rule.json concrete_to/examples before training.

title: short_edit1 decontam drops legitimate short commands en masse
detail: The new rule drops any <=5-token item within token edit distance 1 of ANY eval utterance. For 1-token items that is every 1-token eval ('play','stop','mute','darker' all match DeskMind 'archive'); for 2-3 token items any eval sharing the verb matches ('open chrome'~'open finder', 'kill safari'~'kill bluetooth'). It removes exactly the short voice commands that are the core of the router's traffic, concentrated in open_app (H5 weak label) and open_folder, while catching few true paraphrases.
evidence: repro @80cb13f: Index(decontam.eval_utterances()) (753 repo evals; /data HobbyLM copy absent) over the 1422 unique committed items in training/artifacts (gen_sample2_picked, parity_300, render samples): 62/423 short items dropped by short_edit1 alone (14.7%); open_app 17/34 short, open_folder 13/32, sleep_display 5/32, open_url 4/9, media_control 3/7, mute 3/7. Spurious pairs: 'open chrome'->'open finder' (hobbylm sealed-r1), 'play'/'stop'/'mute'/'darker'->'archive' (deskmind/diag), 'kill safari'->'kill bluetooth' (route_v1), 'make the screen dimmer'->'make the screen brighter'.
fix: Skip len<=1 items; require the differing token to be a near-variant (char edit<=2, e.g. 'her'/'him', 'dot'/'.') or a stopword, not any substitution: `diff_ok = lambda x,y: x in STOP or y in STOP or lev(x,y)<=2`. Report dropped counts per label and abort if any label loses >10% of short items.
